kind: real in-game executions of the per-step pair update, captured by a private bounded plugin at three points inside the step, compared offline with the Python chain

capture_point.routine: 18b8fa0(controller), sole direct caller 18ae2b4 (reached from 140b1a0, called directly by the world step 1389a50); no stored pointer on that path
capture_point.mechanism: object vtable-pointer swap: the broad-phase object at controller+0x28 (vtable image RVA 0x29ca8a0, 34 slots, referenced only by its constructor and destructor) had its vtable pointer compare-exchanged to a private copy of the table with slots +0x60, +0x40 and +0x88 replaced by forwarding detours; heap data write only, no code bytes, no page protections, no change to the shared .rdata table

snapshots.S0: vt+0x60 call (return 18b8ff2): before 18dedf0 select, 18e28d0 rebuild and 18ddc40 pair jobs
snapshots.S1: vt+0x40 call (return 18b902c): after select and rebuild, before pair jobs; includes the caller-local selection vector at caller rsp+0x20
snapshots.S2: vt+0x88 call (return 18b907b): after pair jobs, before the controller+0x4c bump, broad-phase +8 write and 18df490

capture_point.identity_checks: image base; 274-byte fingerprint of 18b8fa0; 64-byte fingerprint of the four getters 19403e0..1940410; all 34 vtable slots equal the image; controller vtable 0x29ca0e0 reached from the player body chain; controller+0x28 vtable pointer equals the image table; detours act only when self is the target object and the return address is the 18b8fa0 call site
capture_point.bounds: armed when a player body first had a controller and a +0x80 head; at most 32 captured steps per session; spacing and minimum-removed filters; per-walk caps 16000 regions / 6 MiB; fixed 160 MiB buffer; self ReadProcessMemory reads; trace written by a worker thread after restore
capture_point.restore: re-check controller+0x28 and that the object still holds the private table, compare-exchange the original table pointer back, wait for in-flight detour calls to drain; module pinned

comparison_method.stage_a_S0_to_S1: Python select_pose_provider_links on the S0 removed rows, then rebuild_pose_body_connectivity (link = remove_pose_group_link, 18e2de0 = recording stub). Selection list compared with the game vector; predicted bytes compared with S1 at every S0-captured address. Group/slot-array/context differences are attributed to 18e2de0 only when Python queued a group; any other difference is unattributed and fails the step.
comparison_method.stage_b_S1_to_S2: structural: publish fields provider+0x170/+0x178, claim cursor +0x17c minus the pair count gives the worker count (bounded by the 18ddc40 formula); the new-link merge (merge_pose_new_links semantics) is checked by count, multiset and comparator order of provider+0x28 against the S2 worker vectors (supplied product of the pair workers), tree membership of every merged link key and ring membership of its endpoints; fate of every selected link; red-black invariants of both provider trees at S0, S1 and S2; a census of S1->S2 changed bytes by region role.

verdict: PASS: 64 captured in-game 18b8fa0 steps (37 with removed rows); stage A 64/64 (selection equal 64, 802 predicted changed bytes matched, 0 unattributed of 1164424 compared); stage B structural 64/64.

negative_controls.note: deliberate bugs injected into the Python side once, then restored (rerun of analyze_step on the same traces)
negative_controls.rebuild_skips_context_counter: stage A failed 34 of 64 steps (every step whose rebuild processed a group)
negative_controls.rebuild_skips_group_link_removal: stage A failed the same 34 steps
negative_controls.selection_takes_only_first_reversed_row: stage A failed 1 of 32 session-2 steps (the only step with two selected links)
negative_controls.merge_comparator_inverted: stage B failed 2 of 32 session-2 steps (merges with links of differing body kinds)

limits: The three snapshots are sequential self-reads on the stepping thread; other threads may run meanwhile, so snapshots are not atomic.

Stage B is structural, not byte-level: retire 18de440, neighbor retire 18de510, free-list rebalance 1989e60, the pair workers (contact generation, link acquire/reinit, filters) and the tree inserts 18de6a0/18de830 ran in game and are not reproduced byte for byte.
The vt+0x40/+0x48 list holds every current overlapping pair (most already have links), not only newly created pairs.
The S2 snapshot precedes the controller counter bump, the broad-phase +8 write and 18df490; those are outside the comparison.
Steps captured were on the player world controller only; removal rows were small (see histograms).
Heap addresses, raw bytes and traces are private and not published.
